title: Analyzing the Rock's "Black Adam" training program
summary: NH dissects the Rock's chest and triceps circuit for Black Adam, as reported by Muscle & Fitness: a body part split of same-muscle giant sets at 10-20 reps. He calls it low-intensity pump work for Instagram that only steroids make productive. He then debunks Hollywood and celebrity myths: 4 am training, chicken-rice-broccoli diets, six meals a day, 10,000 kcal claims and 20 lb of muscle in two months.
claims: The Rock has been on steroids for years, which is why he can train this way and why it won't work for naturals
Body part splits are the worst template for gaining muscle; train several muscle groups per session, especially since chest work also hits triceps and shoulders
'Circuits' almost always mean low intensity and lots of junk volume
With light weights it's hard to reach failure because you can keep pumping forever
Superset antagonists; don't chain three exercises for the same muscle
Supersets that share secondary muscles (stiff-leg deadlift with rows) are poor but acceptable because the main focus differs
Three back-to-back chest exercises could be replaced by one hard set of a horizontal press to failure at low reps, for the same or better result and real progression
As a natural, pump without fibre damage won't grow you; the pump goes away
Do as little volume as possible for as much result as possible: minimum hard sets, building volume from there
You must know your rep ranges so progress can be logged; every rep range needs a reason you can explain
Under 20 reps is not low reps; low reps means under 5-6
Low reps build muscle and drive progression
A triceps-only day makes no sense for such a small muscle
The only advantage of once-a-week body part splits is laziness: minimum work for maximum drug results; even enhanced lifters would grow more with more frequency
Close-grip push-ups followed by overhead extensions is a good superset: lateral head then long head of the triceps
Two kinds of pushdowns back to back hit the same area; pick one
Celebrity workouts are made to be filmed for Instagram and movie promotion; their physiques owe more to chemistry than gym effort
Waking at 3-4 am to train does nothing for muscle or testosterone; total volume and tonnage matter, not the time of day
Chicken, rice and broccoli has nothing special; broccoli is poorly digested by many, and turkey, other veg or sweet potatoes work as well
Not even 5% of naturals need six meals a day; one or two meals are fine if calories and nutrients are met
Celebrities inflate calorie claims like 10,000 kcal and misjudge their body fat; don't let them shape your body image or eating
Gaining 20 lb of muscle in 2-3 months is impossible even on steroids; weight gain always includes fat and water
Natural bodybuilding means looking big all year, not peaking for one moment; avoid yo-yo diets and steroids
The pump makes you big momentarily; proper programming makes you big forever
Showy suffering like 50-rep bench finishers is eye candy that sells programs to novices
A program written on a restaurant napkin by a knowledgeable unknown beats a celebrity program
exercises: Machine fly / incline machine press / dips circuit
same-muscle giant set, low intensity junk volume
one hard low-rep set to failure
lateral then long head; good combo
